name: Pressure Plate
description: The floor-bound sibling of world.switch_mechanism: a switch that reads weight instead of hands. It owns the pressed/released fact on a named channel, the source filter — player, crate, or either — and a release delay, because a plate that flickers as a crate micro-bounces makes every door it feeds stutter. The source filter is the design surface: player-only plates force escort-free solutions, crate-only plates make the crate the key, and any-source plates let the player choose, which is why one component must distinguish all three. It deliberately does not own what the weight triggers; consumers subscribe to the channel exactly as they do for switches. It also does not detect the crate itself — world.pushable_block announces world.block_settled, and this component trusts that fact rather than reimplementing collision.

inputs.name: channelId
inputs.description: The wire name this plate broadcasts on, shared vocabulary with world.switch_mechanism so doors cannot tell — and do not care — which kind of control feeds them.

inputs.name: acceptedSources
inputs.description: player, crate, or any. This single field is the difference between 'stand here while the door opens', 'fetch the crate', and 'your choice'.

inputs.name: requiresContinuousWeight
inputs.description: True releases the plate when weight leaves (hold-the-door puzzles); false latches after first press (a one-way commitment, closer to a switch in spirit).

inputs.name: releaseDelaySeconds
inputs.description: Grace period before an unweighted plate reports released. Absorbs bounce and foot-shuffle so consumers see one clean press instead of a flutter.

outputs.name: pressingSource
outputs.description: What is currently holding the plate — player, crate, or none — so hint systems can say why a crate-only plate ignores the player.
